It's very common for private landlords - not large property management companies, etc. - to get skittish about anything just because their profit margins are a lot thinner than those of corporate properties. Some are very, very picky and only approve applications from nearly perfect candidates. If your application has been approved and the unit has been taken off the market (confirm that with your real estate agent if you have one), then you probably have a little more leverage to negotiate the lease.

That said, most leases I've seen for condos are standard from a regional real estate association. It's just a template. For the landlord to modify it and add a clause, they'd either have to write up a separate amendment to it or create a whole new document, which is a hassle.

Anyway, even with this clause lacking, the policy I've heard of is that you can move out and they will relist the unit, and you're responsible for finding a new tenant until it's rented by someone else. That's not as bad as being locked in for a full year, assuming it gets interest and is rented by someone else within 1-2 months, but still not as great as being able to just show the landlord a great job offer and leave early. That's a privilege generally only afforded at corporate properties that are comfortable with and accustomed to high turnover.

**TL;DR** The landlord probably won't take advantage of you as-is, but you also don't want to sign something if you really, truly don't agree to it, so it's your decision on how to proceed. All in all, if you really think you'll want to leave because a great job offer comes up, private renting may not be the best fit for you.
